newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cr Foncier injection not option - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: Cr Foncier injection not option - Arthuis.

text.p: Finance minister Jean Arthuis said turning French property lender Credit Foncier into a state bank could cost three to five billion francs and he did not believe this was an option.

"Would it be reasonable to create a state-owned bank in the property loans sector? Does the state have the will or the means to create a state bank in a sector which is already fiercely competitive? I believe not," Arthuis said on Tuesday.

"Can we in all decency look for three to five billion francs from taxpayers for such a project, and excluding the risks later on if the profitability of the establishment does not come true? I don't think so," Arthuis told the National Assembly's finance committee.
An advance copy of his address was supplied to Reuters.
Arthuis was defending his plan to wind down Credit Foncier after "nationalising" the group via a takeover by state-owned bank Caisses des Depots et Consignations (CDC).

His wind-down plan, announced after Credit Foncier posted a 1995 loss of 10.8 billion francs, has run into opposition from staff, trade unions and a number of politicians who say Credit foncier is making a profit and would be a viable company if it were recapitalised.
